Synopsis: Our party encounters a band of githyanki warriors who have taken position at bottleneck in the region - a bridge that provides one of the few paths of progression. The gith confront us and try to see if we know anything about the 'weapon' they seek. (The weapon in question is the strange puzzle box we are carrying.) While reading our thoughts, the githyanki may realise we are tadpoled, resulting in instant combat. If we manage to conceal our tadpoles, they may allow us to pass. context: Your party has been stopped at a narrow bridge by a band of githyanki led by the cold commander Kith'rak Voss, who is hunting for a “precious weapon” that fell from a crashed vessel — the strange puzzle box the party now carries. The gith can probe minds (like Detect Thoughts) and will instantly turn violent if they discover the party is tadpoled, so resisting or concealing mental signs is critical to avoid immediate combat. Voss is pragmatic and cruel: if he deems you useful he may spare you but coerce you to hunt survivors and bring him heads and the weapon, otherwise he’ll kill you. How your companions present themselves or any visible ties to local factions can draw attention and influence whether you’re forced into a fight or pressed into service.
